### Executive Summary

A security breach involving fulfillment partner ShipMonk and hardware wallet provider Trezor has exposed approximately 67,000 U.S. customer records. The incident stemmed from the exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability impacting Metabase software.

The breach was initially reported by Rescana on September 6, 2026. Security teams should monitor Metabase deployments for signs of compromise linked to this zero-day activity.

### Technical Impact & Root Cause

The root cause of the exposure is a zero-day vulnerability in Metabase, tracked as CVE-2026-72898. Threat actors leveraged this flaw to gain unauthorized access to internal systems containing customer records.

The full scope of technical exploitation details and specific data fields accessed during the compromise remain unverified based on the available intelligence.

### Mitigation & IOCs

Organizations utilizing Metabase should audit their environments for unauthorized activity and apply relevant security patches for CVE-2026-72898 as vendor updates are released. Specific remediation instructions from the vendor are not yet confirmed in the provided source.
